scope: Pointer and keyboard dock resizing follow each panel's physical track relative to the canvas. Grouped panels and all separately reordered dock arrangements can grow toward or shrink away from the canvas regardless of left/right panel identity.

source_control.runtime_message: fix(editor): resize docks along their canvas track
source_control.push: Normal fast-forward push verified: GitHub branch head equals runtime commit; compare reports 1 ahead and 0 behind.

implementation.root_cause: Pointer resize deltas and keyboard arrow direction previously depended on the panel's left/right identity. Tabbed panel groups and the six supported three-region dock orders can place either panel on either physical side of the canvas, reversing the old direction.
implementation.fix: The existing first-party shell now determines whether a panel is physically left or right of the canvas from visible element geometry, with the saved dock order as a fallback when a panel is not laid out. Pointer resize captures that physical side at pointerdown; keyboard resizing uses the same geometry helper. Dock identity still selects the width token and limits.
implementation.regression: Real Chromium tests cover grouped panels on both sides plus separately reordered left-right-canvas and canvas-right-left tracks for both pointer and keyboard input. They assert width changes toward the canvas, at least 400 CSS px of unobscured canvas, no Page Model writes, and no Save or Publish calls.
implementation.reuse_and_license: Reused the repository's vanilla dock splitter, canvas-safe CSS Grid placement, saved dock-order preference, ARIA splitter contract, and Playwright/Chromium fixture. No external code or dependency was required.
